import html from typing import Optional # Allowed HTML tags for the invitation content (e.g., basic formatting) ALLOWED_TAGS = ["b", "i", "u", "em", "strong", "p", "br", "ul", "ol", "li"] ALLOWED_ATTRIBUTES = {} # No attributes are allowed for security # Predefined HTML template with placeholders INVITATION_FORMAT = """ {event_title} - Invitation

{event_title}

{event_description}
Date: {event_date}
{additional_notes}
You are invited to join us!
""" def _sanitize_html(content: str) -> str: """ Sanitize arbitrary HTML content, allowing only a restricted set of tags. """ # Escape the entire string first to avoid any script injection escaped = html.escape(content, quote=True) # Re-allow only safe tags by unescaping them # Since we escaped all, now we can use bleach to strip tags try: import bleach except ImportError as exc: raise RuntimeError("bleach library is required for HTML sanitization") from exc sanitized = bleach.clean( escaped, tags=ALLOWED_TAGS, attributes=ALLOWED_ATTRIBUTES, strip=True ) return sanitized def create_event_invitation( title: str, description: str, date: str, notes: Optional[str] = None ) -> str: """ Generate a secure HTML invitation for an event. Parameters ---------- title : str The title or name of the event. description : str A comprehensive description (may contain multiple paragraphs and formatting). date : str The scheduled date of the event. notes : Optional[str] Any supplementary information or instructions. Returns ------- str Sanitized HTML string ready for safe display. """ if notes is None: notes = "" # Sanitize each component safe_title = _sanitize_html(title) safe_description = _sanitize_html(description) safe_date = _sanitize_html(date) safe_notes = _sanitize_html(notes) # Render the invitation template html_invitation = INVITATION_FORMAT.format( event_title=safe_title, event_description=safe_description, event_date=safe_date, additional_notes=safe_notes ) return html_invitation
